relatedSnapshot.title: Leads Contacted card shows a lifetime provider count and can exceed Leads Uploaded after a lead list is replaced
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: a workspace owner (workspace "Name 4's Workspace") reports two cold email campaigns as technical faults. "Health & Supplements Manufacturing | Leadership | US | Name 5 (AIA Created)" shows 5,400 leads contacted against 2,955 uploaded; their screenshot of the campaign's Leads tab reads Leads Uploaded 2,955, Leads Contacted 5,400, Leads In Progress 5,281. "Funding | Leadership | US | Name 5 (AIA Created)" shows 294 contacted and no replies. They also report a high number of bounced emails.

Finding: the two figures count different populations. "Leads Contacted" is the outreach provider's lifetime count of unique leads that ever received an email on that campaign (5,400), while "Leads Uploaded" is the leads currently on the campaign (2,955, all added on 14 Sep). The campaign has been sending since 8 July and its lead list has been replaced and trimmed since: provider upload receipts alone record 695 leads accepted on 31 Aug and 2,950 on 14 Sep, and 5,295 campaign-completed-without-reply events exist for this campaign. "Leads In Progress" (5,281) inherits the same mismatch.

The help centre article for the Analytics tab states the Leads Contacted number is capped at total leads uploaded and "can never exceed it". On this campaign it does, so the documented behaviour and the card disagree once a lead list has been replaced.

Sending is unaffected and no customer action is needed for sending to work. The open product question is whether the card should cap or relabel the contacted figure, or the article should describe its lifetime scope.

Reopen if the customer confirms they never removed or replaced the campaign's leads, which would make the count a data defect rather than a scope mismatch.

relatedSnapshot.title: Handle auto-replies with replacement contact emails
relatedSnapshot.description:
Inbox replies can include automatic responses saying a contact has left a company and listing a new email address. The new address cannot be added directly to the lead list, and forwarding only captures the auto-reply instead of the original outreach message.

Requested behavior:

* Allow the replacement email address in the auto-reply to be added directly to the lead list.
* Allow forwarding the original request to the replacement contact instead of only forwarding the auto-reply.

Current workaround is to manually copy the new email address, then go back to scripts and paste an original script into a forwarded email. Without the workaround, the company and lead are lost.

relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Turn an incoming submission into a usable Person and optional Deal. Keep the sales team's existing details, owner and Deal stage, while saving the new submission's answers and source.

**MVP · Pickup order 10 · Name 9 wave 4**

**Can run in parallel with:** ENG-13467, ENG-13474, ENG-13477, ENG-13478. Follow the shared-file ownership rules on the master; start only when this ticket's own blockers are complete.

## What's included

Apply the receipt using the shared person/deal/field commands inside one transaction. Add supplied contact methods without replacing known collections, fill empty profile values only, retain original answers and provenance, and apply only explicitly mapped existing custom fields. Create a Deal only when requested and no conflicting existing primary Deal exists. Link an existing active Deal without moving or reopening it, even if won/lost.

## Blocked by

* ENG-13471 Record incoming submissions and safely identify the right Person
* ENG-13472 Create usable People and Companies through the CRM API
* ENG-13473 Make deal creation and stage changes behave correctly through the API

## How it should work

Persist application result, CRM changes, activity and durable dispatch markers atomically. Separate applied data from pending effect delivery so a retry resumes effects without rewriting CRM. Do not create a note from raw answers or auto-create companies/field definitions.

## Done when

- [ ] New lead creates the configured Person/Deal/fields and existing-record intake preserves sales edits. A deleted primary Deal gives needs_attention, not resurrection or a uniqueness crash. Invalid mapping rolls back all CRM changes. Repeated receipt application cannot repeat record or workflow effects. Missing company is allowed. Answers remain retrievable by receipt ID.
- [ ] Real database new/existing/deleted/terminal-deal cases, rollback, concurrency and crash-after-commit recovery; existing CRM UI confirmation.
- [ ] The changed contract includes its authorization, error behavior, relevant OpenAPI/example updates and regression tests in this PR. Any browser-reachable change receives browser QA; a non-browser slice records why that lane is not applicable and provides direct runtime/database/protocol proof.
- [ ] The PR fits the live review budget, passes applicable CI and independent review, and has exact-head evidence. No follow-up ticket absorbs unfinished safety acceptance.

## Implementation context

One primary Deal per Person is enforced by an unconditional unique index. Current PATCH contact arrays replace collections, which is unsafe to call naively for each form. Name 8 submission ingestion does not perform this CRM transaction.

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: "Personalized Researched Targets" shows "Leads Uploaded 0" while three leads are listed (<domain>)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: the owner of the <domain> workspace opened with "I found a bug" and attached a screenshot of one campaign's Leads tab: "why is this campaign saying no leads are uploaded when I have 3 in there?" A teammate replied that the three leads are present as "Not Yet Contacted" and that the "Leads Uploaded" counter may not populate until the campaign is launched. Campaign from the conversation link: <url:app.acquisity.ai>

## Testable claim

Campaign "Personalized Researched Targets" (draft, never launched) displays "Leads Uploaded 0" while three leads are listed, because the metric subtracts two provider delete receipts that were recorded for leads Company Two never accepted, so one accepted upload is offset by two deletions.

## Evidence

* outreach_campaign <uuid>: status draft, launched_at NULL, Company Two provider <uuid>, provider_campaign_id <uuid> (Company Two status 0, draft). Three outreach_campaign_lead rows, all status not_yet_contacted: two added 2026-09-12 01:30 (both <domain> addresses), one added 2026-09-14 17:33.
* Provider upload receipts (outreach_campaign_activity, metadata.type = provider_upload_receipt): 2026-09-12 00:54 total_sent 2, leads_uploaded 0, skipped_count 2; 2026-09-12 01:30 total_sent 2, leads_uploaded 0, skipped_count 2; 2026-09-14 17:34 total_sent 1, leads_uploaded 1 with created_leads\[0\].id populated. Every skip-reason counter is 0 in all three receipts.
* Provider delete receipts: 2026-09-12 01:36 leads_deleted 1 and 2026-09-12 03:44 leads_deleted 1. No upload receipt had ever recorded an accepted lead at that point, so those two deletions cannot both correspond to accepted uploads. Only one lead was ever accepted by Company Two, so the true provider-accepted count for this campaign is 1, and the card shows 0.
* The card is provider-receipt based by design: OutreachRepository.getCampaignLeadStats returns totalLeads = currentProviderLeadCount when the projection is authoritative, and getProviderUploadReceiptProjection computes Math.max(0, totalLeadsUploaded - totalLeadsDeleted) (apps/web/lib/outreach/db/campaign.ts). apps/web/components/campaigns/detail/tabs/leads/leads-metrics.tsx renders value={stats?.totalLeads || 0} with the provider-accepted tooltip, and apps/web/content/docs/cold-email-agent/campaigns/managing-campaigns/leads.mdx documents the same meaning.
* The delete receipt is not evidence of a provider deletion: process-campaign-remove-leads sets providerLeadRemoved = true whenever provider.removeLead() does not throw, and InstantlyClient.removeLead (apps/web/lib/outreach/Company Two/client.ts:1815) returns successfully without deleting anything when the lead is not found in the campaign.
* Second finding in the same campaign, reported as context rather than as this cause: the two leads Company Two skipped at upload stay in the campaign as ordinary "Not Yet Contacted" rows and will never be emailed, and no "Leads skipped during upload" card appears for provider-side skips (the campaign's last csvUploadStats shows zero skips).
* Blast radius, current query (count date 2026-09-14): of 885 campaigns holding an authoritative provider-receipt projection, 7 campaigns across 7 organizations and 5 creators have recorded provider deletions exceeding recorded provider uploads (6,441 leads of net over-subtraction), so their "Leads Uploaded" under-reports or clamps to 0. This campaign is one of the seven.
* Repository commit read: e75c68fe1da6424e94a149d02d846c2c8becd947.

## Unblock

After the accounting fix this campaign's card should read 1. For the customer's actual problem, the two skipped leads must be re-added or replaced, because Company Two refused them at upload and they will never be emailed from this campaign.

Foreman support operation: recorded under the customer-report creation role.

relatedSnapshot.title: [P2] Optimize outreach manual lead bulk upsert
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Refined implementation brief

*Refined on 2026-07-21. This is the current delivery brief.*

### Outcome

Remove the remaining per-campaign-lead insert, conflict read, update, and status-write fan-out from manual lead uploads while preserving tenant boundaries, metadata, return values, retries, and tombstone behavior.

### Scope

* Keep the existing organization-lead bulk insert, existing-lead load, cross-campaign filter, and campaign-lead preload.
* Before any write when a campaign ID is supplied, verify inside the repository transaction that the campaign belongs to the repository organization and is not archived through either its display status or legacy lifecycle status. Completed campaigns remain eligible because the current upload flow can reactivate them after leads are linked.
* Name 18 campaign-lead candidates by email before conflict handling and preserve the current first-input-wins behavior.
* Build final campaign-lead rows in memory from the first input row, organization lead, and preloaded campaign-lead row.
* Persist campaign leads in bounded bulk upsert chunks. The exact unique conflict identity is `(campaign_id, email)`.
* Restrict every conflict update to an existing campaign-lead row whose `organization_id` matches the repository organization. Return `id`, `email`, and `organization_id`, then require exactly one organization-matching returned row for every deduplicated campaign-lead candidate.
* Merge stored JSONB metadata first and sanitized incoming metadata second so new manual batch and custom-variable values retain current precedence.
* Preserve stored `espCode` and `esgCode` when the incoming value is null.
* Preassign an application UUID only to each candidate-new campaign lead. Map returned rows by email and compare IDs with the candidate UUID map. Never infer insertion from PostgreSQL return order, input position, or the preload alone.
* Bulk insert `not_yet_contacted` status rows only for true inserts and keep the existing status conflict guard.
* Preserve current soft-deleted campaign-lead conflict behavior. Re-import updates the existing row without clearing `deleted_at`, does not seed a new status row, and does not report the row as newly inserted. Restoring or skipping tombstoned rows requires a separate product decision.
* Preserve `created`, `skipped`, `skippedCrossCampaign`, `linked`, `leads`, `insertedCampaignLeadIds`, activity creation, and transaction behavior.
* Remove the post-write batch-ID verification query. Use bulk-write results for aggregate verification and do not log lead emails or metadata payloads.
* Exclude provider dispatch, email normalization changes, cross-campaign policy changes, schema and index changes, and caller or workflow redesign.

### Acceptance criteria

* A wrong-organization, archived-display, or legacy-archived campaign ID is rejected before the transaction writes organization leads, campaign leads, status rows, or activity.
* The campaign-lead conflict target is exactly `(campaign_id, email)`. Tenant safety comes from repository campaign ownership validation, an organization-restricted conflict update, and the returned-row invariant.
* Every deduplicated candidate produces exactly one returned row with the expected email and organization. A missing, duplicate, unexpected, or wrong-organization returned row aborts the transaction.
* Campaign-lead write queries grow by bounded chunks rather than by lead count. Each chunk performs one campaign-lead upsert and at most one bulk status insert.
* No per-lead conflict lookup, per-lead update, or per-lead status insert remains.
* Existing metadata keys survive unless the current sanitized incoming value intentionally replaces the same key.
* Existing `preview_env` handling, blocked user custom-variable keys, `manualBatchId`, contact fields, and provider codes retain current precedence.
* New campaign leads receive exactly one `not_yet_contacted` status row and appear in `insertedCampaignLeadIds`.
* Existing leads, replayed leads, soft-deleted conflicts, and concurrent conflict winners do not appear in `insertedCampaignLeadIds` and do not receive a newly seeded status row.
* Duplicate input emails retain current first-input-wins behavior before conflict handling.
* Replaying the same batch is idempotent and preserves current created, skipped, linked, cross-campaign, activity, and return semantics.
* Batch logs contain organization, campaign, batch, and count context but no emails or metadata values.

### Implementation direction

Validate the target campaign at the start of the repository transaction when a campaign ID is present. Use the existing preloaded campaign-lead map to resolve final values. Keep a single first-seen map across the full input so deduplication does not reset at chunk boundaries.

Give each candidate-new row an application UUID, then issue bounded `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (campaign_id, email) DO UPDATE` chunks. Restrict the update arm to rows owned by the repository organization. Set ordinary columns from the incoming row, merge metadata as stored JSONB followed by incoming JSONB, and coalesce nullable provider codes against stored values.

Return `id`, `email`, and `organization_id`. Validate cardinality and tenant ownership before mapping by email. Compare each returned ID with the candidate UUID map to identify true inserts. Seed statuses only from that verified insert set.

Keep tombstoned conflicts tombstoned. Do not add `deleted_at` to the unique identity, clear it during upsert, or turn re-import into an implicit restore.

### Dependencies

* PR #5463 is a hard implementation sequencing gate because it is open and changes `campaign.ts`, the shared repository database test file, and campaign-lead dispatch behavior.
* Do not start implementation while PR #5463 is open. After it merges or closes, refresh `main`, re-inventory this method and its tests, then implement on that terminal result.
* Follow parent ENG-10465 by keeping this outreach repository child separate from ENG-10470, ENG-10473, and ENG-10474 rather than implementing them concurrently.

### Validation

* Extend the database-backed outreach repository suite for all-new, all-existing, mixed, replay, concurrent-winner, duplicate-input, wrong-organization campaign, archived campaign, and tombstoned conflict cases.
* Deliberately reorder returned rows and verify mapping is independent of database return order.
* Cover metadata precedence, custom-variable sanitization, `preview_env`, `manualBatchId`, null `espCode` and `esgCode` retention, and status creation only for true inserts.
* Assert exact status cardinality and exact `created`, `skipped`, `skippedCrossCampaign`, `linked`, `leads`, and `insertedCampaignLeadIds` parity.
* Compare inputs below and above the campaign-lead chunk boundary and prove query growth is bounded by chunk count.
* Re-read the terminal PR #5463 result and current `main` before implementation.
* Confirm no migration or index change is introduced.

## Original description

Source audit section: `n+1.md` P2 outreach manual lead bulk upsert.

Scope:

* `apps/web/lib/outreach/db/campaign.ts`
* Callers in `apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/leads.ts`
* Workflow callers in outreach workflow step files

Problem:
`bulkUpsertManualCampaignLeads` chunks input but still does per-lead insert, conflict lookup, metadata merge, and update work.

Acceptance criteria:

* Preload existing campaign leads for all input emails in one query.
* Merge metadata in memory.
* Bulk insert new leads.
* Reduce conflicting row updates with chunked or SQL-level JSONB merge where practical.
* Bulk insert matching lead status rows for newly inserted leads.

relatedSnapshot.title: Cold email agent: per-campaign enable seeds correct defaults + pause must pair with replacement
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When the cold email agent looks at a campaign that isn't working, it's supposed to pause that campaign AND immediately spin up a fresh replacement (new leads, new copy) to take its place. The problem was that it could recommend pausing a campaign on its own, with no replacement lined up, so a live campaign would just stop and nothing would run after it. Separately, turning the agent on for a campaign could quietly reset choices a user had already made, and the custom threshold boxes were fiddly to edit and wouldn't accept decimals like 0.5%. This change makes a pause always come with a real replacement, protects existing settings when the agent is switched on, and makes the threshold inputs behave like normal number fields.

## Problem

**Pause could happen without a replacement (the main issue).**

* The decision prompt described "create a new campaign" as loose prose rather than a required paired action, and there was no server-side guard, so the agent could emit (or recommend) a standalone `PAUSE_CAMPAIGN`. (`packages/ai/src/prompts/campaign/campaign-decision.ts`)
* The pause-pairing guard only ran for `borderline`/`underperforming` statuses (`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/util/campaign-agent-approval-flow.ts`), but the decision schema lets any status carry any action and the prompt says the rule applies to every status — so a pause emitted under `healthy`/`too_early` bypassed the guard entirely.
* Even when a `START_NEW_CAMPAIGN` was present, the pause executed based only on the per-action setting, with no dependency on whether the replacement actually got created. The start could be skipped at runtime (no lead plan / usage limit / blocked plan / no user) while the pause still ran independently (`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/process-campaign-analytics.ts`). Net result: a live campaign paused with nothing to replace it.

**Enabling the agent could overwrite existing config.** The first-enable seed gate only checked for an `approvalModes` object, so campaigns configured before that field existed (real action booleans, no `approvalModes`) were treated as unconfigured and overwritten with the recommended preset. (`apps/web/components/campaigns/detail/tabs/options/campaign-settings-card.tsx`, `apps/web/lib/outreach/campaign-agent-approval-modes.ts`)

**Thresholds: weak validation + clunky inputs + migration churn.** `booked_call_threshold` is an integer DB column but the tRPC inputs accepted any number with no bounds, and PRR min/max were only enforced in the UI (`apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/settings.ts`). The inline threshold number inputs snapped back to `min` on every keystroke and rejected decimals like `0.5`. Making PRR decimal-capable had shipped as two migrations plus a hash-restore commit.

## Solution / What changed

* **Prompt** (`campaign-decision.ts`): the pause-pairing rule is MANDATORY and "applies to every status"; the borderline and underperforming branches explicitly emit `START_NEW_CAMPAIGN` in the same actions list as the pause; if a replacement can't be justified, the agent must not pause and explains why instead.
* **Guard** (`campaign-agent-approval-flow.ts`): `enforceCampaignPausePairing` is now status-independent — it unconditionally drops any `PAUSE_CAMPAIGN` that has no enabled, executable `START_NEW_CAMPAIGN`, drops the accompanying `DISABLE_VARIANTS`, and sanitizes the human-facing reason/recommendation copy so removed pauses aren't described to the user.
* **Execution** (`process-campaign-analytics.ts`): a pause is now deferred and only runs after all start actions have executed, and only if a replacement campaign was actually created this run (confirmed from the campaign-creator submission result, not just "the step ran"). If the replacement is skipped for any reason — no leads, usage limit, blocked plan, no user, no created campaign id — the pause is skipped and the campaign is left running. If the agent feature is turned off mid-approval, every eligible pause is marked skipped. The manual/user-initiated pause is a separate path and is untouched.
* **Seed gate** (`campaign-agent-approval-modes.ts` + `campaign-settings-card.tsx`): a new `shouldSeedRecommendedAgentDefaults` seeds the recommended preset only when there is neither an `approvalModes` object nor any explicit legacy action choice, checked on both the campaign's own settings and the inherited org/provider default.
* **Threshold validation** (`settings.ts` + `cold-email-agent-settings-page-client.tsx`): server-side bounds on both save paths (healthy reply rate 0.1–10, winner reply rate 0.1–20, booked-call target integer 1–100) matching the DB column types, plus an integer constraint on the booked-call UI field.
* **Threshold input UX** (`campaign-settings-card.tsx` number input, `form-input.tsx`): the field holds an in-progress draft while editing, clamps only on blur, supports a per-field step, and accepts decimals.
* **Schema/migration** (`outreach.ts` + migrations): healthy/winner reply-rate columns are decimal (`real`), booked-call stays integer, collapsed into a single migration.

## Scope

In scope: per-campaign agent enable seeding; pause-must-pair-with-replacement across prompt, guard, and execution; decimal threshold persistence + server-side validation; threshold input editing UX; a single DB migration.

Out of scope: no production backfill or heal of existing rows (forward-only); manual/user-initiated pause behavior is unchanged; the borderline branch keeps its pause-and-replace behavior (not changed to optimise-and-wait); a truly legacy "all actions off" config (no `approvalModes`, every action false) is indistinguishable from a never-configured campaign and may be re-seeded with the recommended preset.

## Acceptance criteria

* A standalone agent pause never surfaces or executes on any status; a lone `PAUSE_CAMPAIGN` (and its accompanying `DISABLE_VARIANTS`) is dropped and the user-facing copy is sanitized.
* A pause executes only when a paired replacement campaign was actually created this run; if the replacement is skipped at runtime, the campaign keeps running and the pause is recorded as skipped.
* Manual/user-initiated pause still works exactly as before.
* Enabling the agent on a campaign with no agent config seeds the recommended preset: optimise-variants runs automatically, and add-leads / create-campaign / pause are ask-first.
* Enabling the agent never overwrites an existing `approvalModes` config or a legacy config with any action enabled, whether campaign-scoped or inherited.
* Healthy and winner reply-rate thresholds accept and persist decimals (e.g. 0.5); booked-call target rejects non-integers and out-of-range values on the server.
* Threshold inputs can be cleared and edited freely, clamp only on blur, and percentage fields accept sub-1 values.
* Exactly one new DB migration ships and the snapshot chain validates.

## How to QA (non-developer)

1. Simulate an agent decision on an underperforming campaign with plenty of data → it proposes pausing the old campaign AND creating a new one together, never a pause on its own.
2. Force a situation where the replacement can't run (e.g. no leads available) → the campaign is NOT paused; it keeps running.
3. On a campaign that already had agent action choices, toggle the agent off and back on → the previous choices are preserved, not reset.
4. Enable the agent on a brand-new campaign → it starts with optimise-variants on automatic and the bigger actions set to ask-first.
5. In custom thresholds: clear a box and type a new value → it doesn't snap back while you type; enter 0.5 in a reply-rate field → accepted; try a decimal in the booked-call target → rejected.
6. Pause a campaign yourself (manual) → still works exactly as before.

relatedSnapshot.title: Leads Section Update, Fixes & UI Overhaul
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The Leads tab has accumulated several gaps that make some important  day-to-day campaign operations impossible:

* No ability to filter or select not yet contacted leads to export/delete them
* Filters are complicated and don't work
* bulk selection and bulk actions do not work cleanly across pages
* the toolbar and columns are not optimized for common review/export workflows
* adding leads manually or via CSV is more limited than the underlying product needs
* Make the add leads button clear and stand out
* Adding leads with AI search is hidden and hard to find

This work packages those improvements into one parent issue so the end-to-end Leads experience can be shipped in an ordered way.

## Solution

Deliver the Leads overhaul as three sub-issues that should merge in sequence:

1. ENG-7757 — lead status system
2. ENG-7758 — cross-page selection, bulk actions, toolbar, column order
3. ENG-7759 — add leads modal, manual lead entry, CSV field improvements

## Scope

### PR 1 — Lead status system

* Clean up status naming by replacing legacy `active` and `replied` handling with `not_yet_contacted` and `reply_received`
* Migrate and backfill status history so leads without history rows still participate in filtering and display
* Add a status dropdown with explicit filter modes for untouched leads, latest effective status, and inclusive history matching
* Compute latest effective status using send-vs-response precedence instead of raw timestamp ordering
* Show multiple statuses per lead with clipped inline badges and tooltip overflow
* Extend CSV export with `latestStatus`, `allStatuses`, and `statusUpdatedAt`
* Ensure preview data includes status-history data needed for validation

### 

* Support cross-page selection from the header checkbox with both "Select all" and "Select this page"
* Move bulk actions into the toolbar and make labels/counts contextual to the current selection
* Redesign the toolbar layout to better support search, filtering, status filtering, delete, export, and add-lead actions
* Reorder columns to match the intended lead-review workflow
* Add tooltips that only appear when cell content is actually truncated

### PR 3 — Add leads and CSV improvements

* Replace the current import entry point with a unified "+ Add Leads" modal
* Support three entry paths: AI search, CSV import, and manual single-lead entry
* Expand manual lead entry with the required set of fields for realistic lead creation
* Make `website` and `companyDescription` first-class CSV-mapped fields instead of custom variables
* Accept domain-style URLs by auto-prepending `https://` where appropriate
* Ensure manually entered metadata is surfaced correctly in the leads table

## UX behavior

* The parent issue tracks the whole Leads overhaul, while implementation detail lives in the three sub-issues
* The merge order matters because later work depends on the status and toolbar foundations being in place

relatedSnapshot.title: Campaign CSV lead import silently corrupts non-UTF-8 files into replacement characters
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Uploading a lead CSV whose file encoding is not UTF-8 (for example Excel's plain "CSV (comma delimited)" export, which is Windows-1252) stores every accented or otherwise non-ASCII character as the Name 23 replacement character (U+FFFD). The import reports success, so the corruption is silent: names and any mapped custom-variable copy (for example per-lead Spanish email bodies) land in the campaign audience already mangled, and the sequence renders the placeholder glyphs.

## Problem

A customer uploads a Spanish-language lead list with accented names and per-lead copy, the import completes without an error, and the audience and sequence preview read as "Name 24, ... Company Six estn ... vehculos". Nothing in the UI or the help center tells the operator the file's encoding matters.

## Root cause

The campaign CSV import decodes the uploaded file as UTF-8 and substitutes U+FFFD for any byte sequence it cannot decode, with no encoding detection, fallback, warning, or refusal. The decode happens in the browser: apps/web/components/crm/spreadsheet-import/utils/parse-csv.ts -> parseCsv() calls Papa.parse(file, {...}) with no `encoding` option (steps/upload-step.tsx handleFileChange is the caller), so Papa streams the File through FileReader.readAsText with its UTF-8 default. The campaign lead upload reaches it through apps/web/components/campaigns/campaign-import-client.tsx (SpreadsheetImportFlow, entityType "leadUpload"). The mangled values are then written verbatim by the campaign audience write path (apps/web/lib/outreach/db/campaign.ts, bulk add / manual link of firstName, lastName, metadata, customVariables, metadata.manuallyAdded: true), which does not validate or normalize the bytes.

## Blast radius

Counted 2026-09-23. Unscoped: `select count(distinct organization_id), count(*) from outreach_campaign_lead where first_name ~ U&'\FFFD' or last_name ~ U&'\FFFD'` -> 24 organizations, 195 audience rows with a replacement character in the lead name (a lower bound: the query covers names only). Of those, 120 rows across 14 organizations carry metadata.manuallyAdded = true and are confirmed attribution to this code path; the remaining 75 rows across roughly 10 organizations have unverified provenance and may indicate a second write path worth checking. Reporting workspace: two unlaunched draft campaigns with 224 audience rows, 206 of them carrying corrupted per-lead copy; 0 emails sent, so no delivery has been affected.

## Proposed fix

Read the uploaded file with an explicit encoding strategy instead of assuming UTF-8: honour a UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM, fall back to Windows-1252/Latin-1 when the bytes are not valid UTF-8, and when neither is possible refuse the file with an explicit error naming the encoding problem. Never write U+FFFD into stored lead data. Optionally extend the "Importing leads via CSV" help article with the encoding requirement.

## What's included

Decode handling at the single parse seam plus a regression test. Customer-side recovery (re-export as UTF-8 and re-import, which updates the existing audience rows in place) is covered by the attached report and needs no engineering work; no Acquisity-side record repair is possible because the per-lead copy exists only in the customer's original file. Observability: nothing currently counts imports that contained undecodable bytes, so a warning or counter at the parse seam is worth adding.

## Regression seam

parseCsv (apps/web/components/crm/spreadsheet-import/utils/parse-csv.ts) with a Windows-1252 fixture containing accented characters: red today (accents become U+FFFD with no error), green after the fix (accents preserved, or a clear refusal for a genuinely undecodable file).

## Done when

* A Windows-1252 CSV with accented names imports with the accents intact, and no U+FFFD is written to outreach_campaign_lead.
* A file that cannot be decoded in any supported encoding fails with an explicit, user-visible error instead of importing silently corrupted values.
* A regression test proves the mechanism at the parse seam.

## Reports

* ENG-14194

relatedSnapshot.title: Replace Routine CRM Analysis With Deterministic Rules
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Replace routine CRM conversation analysis with explicit rules using campaign lead data, existing reply classification and confirmed appointment events.

Users keep the outcomes that matter, while routine CRM sync stops sending full email threads to a model.

## Delivery order

**Urgent Ticket 2.**

* **Blocked by:** ENG-12418 - Switch CRM Sync From Gemini Pro to GPT-5.6 Luna.
* **Next:** ENG-12421 - Measure and Roll Out Deterministic CRM Sync.
* **Parallel follow-up:** ENG-12420 - Make Contact and Deal Updates Atomic may start after this ticket.

## What to build

Replace the internals of the central CRM sync path without requiring callers to adopt a new public entry point.

Deterministic inputs:

* Contact name, email, title and company from explicit user overrides and persisted campaign lead data.
* Pipeline from the campaign where configured.
* Reply outcome from the existing reply classification.
* Appointment status and call type from the confirmed appointment record.
* Probability from the selected CRM stage.
* Amount remains empty when no structured amount exists.

Required stage behavior:

* Clear positive interest may move a non-terminal automated deal to one unique interested or positive-response stage.
* A confirmed appointment may advance a non-terminal deal to the exact booked stage for its call type.
* An explicit decline or do-not-contact outcome may use one unique declined, lost or unqualified stage.
* Out-of-office, referral and generic acknowledgements do not advance a deal.
* Routine replies never move a human-controlled stage.
* No event regresses a deal or reopens Won/Lost.
* Unknown or ambiguous stage mappings leave the stage unchanged and emit a stable reason code.
* There is no model fallback when a deterministic rule cannot decide.

This ticket keeps the temporary Luna path available only as the controlled rollback path used by ENG-12421. Atomic contact-and-deal persistence remains separately owned by ENG-12420.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Routine CRM sync sends no full email thread for contact or deal analysis.
- [ ] Name 25 name, email, title and company fields come from structured lead data.
- [ ] Interested, booked and declined outcomes follow explicit stage rules.
- [ ] Out-of-office, referral and generic replies do not advance.
- [ ] Human-controlled stages remain protected during routine replies.
- [ ] A confirmed appointment can advance to the exact booked stage without removing the manual lock.
- [ ] Won/Lost deals are never reopened.
- [ ] Unknown stages are safe no-ops and never trigger a paid fallback.
- [ ] Every applied or preserved field has a stable reason code.
- [ ] Production-shaped fixtures cover duplicate events, missing data, manual stages, terminal stages, unknown stages and appointment events.
- [ ] All existing CRM callers continue through the same central entry point.

## Blocked by

* ENG-12418 - Switch CRM Sync From Gemini Pro to GPT-5.6 Luna
